analysis.title: KLA Corp. (KLAC): Improving growth and execution against accelerating industry trends
key_insights: GS expects KLAC to trade modestly higher after a quarter and 4Q guidance above the Street, with investor positioning slightly negatively biased after Lam's print despite more bullish consensus WFE forecasts.
Reported 3Q26 (Sep quarter) revenue was $4.14bn, below GS at $4.22bn and above the Street (Visible Alpha) at $4.04bn. Revenue grew 31.4% y/y and 15.4% q/q.
Non-GAAP EPS of $1.22 was below GS at $1.25 and above the Street at $1.18. Gross margin of 62.7% compared with GS 62.5% and Street 62.6%. Operating margin was 46.1%.
Systems revenue of $3.29bn was below GS at $3.38bn and above the Street at $3.23bn. Service revenue of $851mn was above GS at $844mn and in line with the Street at $853mn.
Y/Y revenue growth accelerated in the quarter, helped in part by easing supply chain constraints, against a backdrop of accelerating WFE (wafer fab equipment) growth that GS expects.

KLA management raised its 2026 total WFE outlook to ~$155bn including advanced packaging, from the low-$150bn range. For 2027 it now expects $200bn (+~30% y/y), up from $190bn (+25% y/y). Management believes it can meet or exceed 30% growth in CY27 as supply constraints ease.
KLA sees sequential revenue growth through CY27, with memory a larger share of its mix than in prior years.

Advanced packaging: management still expects CY26 advanced packaging process control systems revenue of $1.1bn (+70% y/y), which it says is nearly double the market growth rate. Continued share gains and SAM expansion should support growth.

Margins: gross margin trends have improved despite DRAM cost headwinds, and management is comfortable sustaining gross margin at or above current levels. OpEx is guided up $20-25mn q/q in CY4Q, and management targets 40%-50% incremental margin drop-through in the medium term.

4Q26 guidance midpoint: revenue $4.70bn (GS $4.60bn, Street $4.49bn), gross margin 62.5% (GS 62.3%, Street 62.6%), non-GAAP EPS $1.44 (GS $1.41, Street $1.36). Guided revenue is +46.4% y/y at the high end, +36.1% at the midpoint.
GS raises CY26-28 EPS estimates by an average of 5% on higher revenue and operating margin assumptions. CY27E EPS goes to $6.50 from $6.05 and CY28E to $8.00 from $7.45.
GS trims its price target to $195 from $210, based on 30x P/E (down from 32x on lower peer multiples) applied to unchanged normalized EPS of $6.50.

GS stays Neutral. It sees KLA as a dominant franchise with a market share advantage in process control, but does not expect process control to outgrow WFE spending near term and sees valuation as relatively full.

GS prefers Buy-rated AMAT and LRCX, which have more exposure to etch and deposition, the beneficiaries of the industry shift toward higher near-term DRAM spending. GS expects a neutral reaction for AMAT and LRCX.

market_movers.rationale: Target cut from $210 as the P/E multiple falls to 30x from 32x on lower peer multiples, while normalized EPS stays at $6.50. Valuation is seen as relatively full and process control is not expected to outgrow WFE near term.
Preferred over KLAC for greater etch and deposition exposure as DRAM spending rises. Neutral reaction expected to KLA's print.
Preferred over KLAC for greater etch and deposition exposure as DRAM spending rises. Neutral reaction expected to KLA's print.

sector_views.rationale: WFE growth is accelerating, with KLA seeing $155bn in 2026 and $200bn in 2027. GS favors etch and deposition names over process control because of the near-term shift to DRAM spending.

earnings_insights: KLAC 3Q26 (Sep quarter, reported 10/28): revenue $4.14bn reported vs GS $4.22bn and Street (Visible Alpha) $4.04bn. Non-GAAP EPS $1.22 reported vs GS $1.25 and Street $1.18. Gross margin 62.7% and operating margin 46.1%.

KLAC 4Q26 guidance midpoint (range $4.5bn-$4.9bn): revenue $4.70bn vs GS estimate $4.60bn and Street estimate $4.49bn. Non-GAAP EPS $1.44 (range $1.33-$1.55) vs GS estimate $1.41 and Street estimate $1.36. Gross margin 62.5% vs GS estimate 62.3% and Street estimate 62.6%.
GS estimates revenue of $16,012mn for CY26 (+25.6% y/y), $20,766mn for CY27 (+29.7%) and $24,744mn for CY28 (+19.2%). GS non-GAAP EPS estimates are $4.70, $6.50 and $8.00 for CY26-28.
GS fiscal-year (June) estimates: EPS $5.84 for FY27E (old $5.58) and $7.12 for FY28E (old $6.61). Quarterly EPS estimates are $1.48 for Dec 2026, $1.54 for Mar 2027 and $1.60 for Jun 2027.
risk_factors: Uncertainty related to export restrictions if they were removed.

vol_and_positioning: GS believes investor positioning in KLAC is slightly negatively biased after Lam's print, despite more bullish consensus WFE spending forecasts.
geopolitical: The report lists US export restrictions as a risk: incremental restrictions would hurt, and uncertainty if existing restrictions were removed.

tension_points.bull_case: KLA has best-in-class products, a significant share advantage over its nearest process control competitor, accelerating y/y growth, and WFE seen at $200bn in 2027 (+30%). Share gains in advanced packaging add to growth.
tension_points.bear_case: GS does not expect process control to outgrow WFE spending near term, valuation is relatively full, and the shift to DRAM favors etch and deposition names.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A sharp increase in Foundry/Logic spending, or a sharp rebound in Memory WFE spending relative to Foundry/Logic, are the listed risks to GS's view.
